clusters.label: Multi-supplier lead-time consolidation picks the wrong supplier
clusters.root_cause_hypothesis: Standing-order scheduler resolves lead time across suppliers with the wrong aggregate (shortest instead of longest), so orders land late for one account and early for another.
clusters.evidence: TRQ-1046 notes 'not picking the longest lead-time item correctly when an order spans multiple suppliers'; TRQ-1060 notes 'shortest lead time across suppliers instead of the longest' and explicitly calls it the inverse of TRQ-1046.

clusters.label: Standing-order scheduler fails silently with no alerting
clusters.root_cause_hypothesis: Scheduler task can fail without raising an error or notification; TRQ-1053 is confirmed, TRQ-1068 has the same signature. Immediate fix is alerting on scheduler failures; the scheduler root cause is a second, separate item.
clusters.evidence: TRQ-1053: 'scheduler task that silently failed with no alerting'; TRQ-1068: 'skip a scheduled week entirely with no failure notification' and notes 'similar signature to TRQ-1053'.

clusters.label: Catalog tag / commodity-code mismatches across accounts
clusters.root_cause_hypothesis: Supplier catalog tags drift from operator commodity codes, especially after catalog migrations and on seasonal SKUs. Not one bug; one recurring data-quality pattern with the same fix path (bulk re-tag now, self-serve tooling later).
clusters.evidence: TRQ-1044 (40+ SKUs, reorder suggestions wrong), TRQ-1052 (seasonal produce, 'possibly a systemic tagging issue'), TRQ-1066 (~200 SKUs after supplier migration). TRQ-1063 notes the pattern is 'seen across nearly every account this quarter'.

clusters.label: ERP timeout + retry creates duplicate orders
clusters.root_cause_hypothesis: When a customer ERP times out, Trellis (or the ERP) retries and the order is submitted twice. Likely fix is idempotency keys on order submission, which covers both accounts regardless of whose retry fires.
clusters.evidence: TRQ-1043: 'retry logic firing when Northwind's ERP times out'; TRQ-1054: 'SAP integration is timing out intermittently, causing orders to be submitted twice'. Both are duplicate-order-on-timeout.

clusters.label: Trellis-side rate-limit configuration gaps
clusters.root_cause_hypothesis: Both are our own rate-limit settings (a month-end limit and an allowlist). No code change; configuration work that should be owned by support or infra with a same-week SLA.
clusters.evidence: TRQ-1049: 'looks like our own rate-limit config, not their retry behavior'; TRQ-1062: 'Configuration gap, not a bug'.

clusters.label: Inventory status shown to buyers does not match availability
clusters.root_cause_hypothesis: Inventory sync lag or flakiness lets out-of-stock or backordered items show as in stock. Two accounts of very different size report it, which supports the 'broader sync-flakiness pattern' guess in TRQ-1047. Cause is unknown; needs a discovery spike before an effort estimate is credible.
clusters.evidence: TRQ-1047: 'inventory status shown to their buyers doesn't match what's actually available'; TRQ-1058: 'seeing in stock items that are actually backordered'.

cross_record_observations: 27 tickets reduce to roughly 8 root causes plus a handful of singletons. TRQ-1046 and TRQ-1060 are one lead-time bug; TRQ-1053 and TRQ-1068 are one silent-failure pattern; TRQ-1043 and TRQ-1054 are one duplicate-order mechanism.

Tag-mapping complaints come from four of the five accounts (TRQ-1044, 1052, 1059, 1066). No single ticket is critical; the pattern is. TRQ-1063 is the only proactive item that directly retires a reactive cluster.
Two tickets marked URGENT by the account (TRQ-1050, TRQ-1061) affect under 2% of orders or a handful of transactions per week by Trellis's own logs. Stated urgency and measured impact disagree.
Two items (TRQ-1049, TRQ-1062) are Trellis-side configuration, not bugs, and have been waiting weeks. That is a support/infra ownership gap, not a roadmap question.

Inventory-sync mismatches appear on both the smallest account (TRQ-1047) and an enterprise account (TRQ-1058), which is the strongest evidence in the backlog for a systemic issue with no identified cause.

The proactive items with the best case (TRQ-1063, TRQ-1057) have no external advocate; the reactive items with the loudest advocates (TRQ-1050, TRQ-1061, TRQ-1049) are among the smallest by measured impact.
